_schema.purpose: Register of every point where corpus_v1 diverges from published scholarship (Younger). Policy S6: adopt the source reading, never silently patch, log everything so results can be re-run under either reading.
_schema.sweep: sweep1 (automated, corpus_v1 vs Younger commentary tables)
_schema.comparison_basis: canonicalised labels with documented convention aliases folded; see sweep1.py

sweep1_summary.caveat: Residual includes some unresolved convention noise. The classified families below are the defensible signal; the presence/absence bucket is dominated by tokenisation and alignment artefacts and is NOT a divergence claim.
comparator_corrections: vessel signs: repo labels A402-VAS as '*815' and writes the VAS suffix as '-VS'; ligature '+' marking differs. Rendering our side from the sign id and stripping ligature notation removed 20 false divergences and raised agreement 91.4% -> 92.0%.

divergences.title: AB21 / AB22 systematic disagreement (sheep vs goats)
divergences.alt_source: Younger, Linear A Texts & Inscriptions in Phonetic Transcription
divergences.semantic_stake: AB21 = QI/OVIS (sheep); AB22 = CAP (goats). Livestock species assignment.
divergences.note: Originally logged as a single conflict at HT 20. The sweep shows it is systematic: it recurs across Haghia Triada, Khania, Knossos, Phaistos and Zakros, and runs in BOTH directions. This is not a transcription slip in one tablet but a standing disagreement over a confusable sign pair.
divergences.adjudicable_by: GORILA plates per document; SigLA palaeographical charts for AB21 vs AB22
affects: all livestock counts and species ratios
sign frequency for AB21 and AB22
divergences.policy_applied: source reading retained corpus-wide; no selective patching

resolution.result: SigLA agrees with Younger on 15 of 15 attestable sites, in BOTH directions
resolution.verdict: Our source (Douros via mwenge) is the outlier. Every AB21/AB22 reading in the D4 set should be inverted to Younger/SigLA. Note this is a systematic inversion, not scattered error: wherever we read AB021 they read AB022 and vice versa, with no exceptions, which points to a systematic mis-mapping in the Douros tabulation rather than 15 independent misreadings.
resolution.caveat: SigLA does not record the M/F gender variants our source carries, so the comparison is at AB21/AB22 family level only. PH(?)31a and PH(?)31b are not in SigLA and remain unadjudicated.
resolution.action_required: corpus_v1 should invert AB021<->AB022 on these 12 documents, or the affected analyses be re-run under both readings

divergences.title: Numeral disagreements
divergences.note: Small in number but disproportionately important: these feed the accounting analysis directly, and HT10a (14 vs 104) is an order-of-magnitude difference.

divergences.title: Other single-sign reading disagreements
divergences.note: Long tail, mostly singletons. Includes KI+*23 vs KI+ME, *307+*387 vs *307+*307, *401+RO vs *401+RA. Some residual convention noise is expected in this bucket; each site needs individual adjudication before use.

triage.method: Three-way vote: our source vs Younger vs SigLA, on sign NUMBER. Sites are testable only where the conflict is sign-type (not fraction/numeral, which sweep 3 showed SigLA under-records) and the document is in SigLA.
triage.headline: Of 84 testable sites, only 9 survive as genuine sign conflicts. The rest are convention artefacts: number-vs-name (HIDE = *180, MU = *23, SO = *363, PU3 = *314), tokenisation of ligatures, or annotation markers. D8 as originally logged was inflated roughly nine-fold by comparator convention, not by disagreement.

sigla_adjudication.note: Where SigLA can adjudicate a single-sign conflict it backs our source more often than Younger, 11 to 2. This is the opposite of D4 and worth stating: our source is not globally unreliable, it had one systematic error. The two sites where SigLA backs Younger are HT132 (*904 vs *319) and PH8a (*416L2 vs *417L2).

divergences.title: Word-boundary disagreements in the religious corpus
divergences.note: Same signs, different boundaries. ALL occur on Z-type supports (the religious corpus). Word division is the Douros contribution, not GORILA, and it is the primary evidence for morphological segmentation of the libation formula. Affected vocabulary includes DU-PU2-RE and U-NA-KA-NA-SI, both core formula terms.
divergences.adjudicable_by: GORILA plates: presence or absence of a word-divider dot at the contested ridge
affects: Duhoux-style agglutination measures, which are boundary-sensitive
divergences.policy_applied: source reading retained; no boundaries altered

resolution_path.source: SigLA JSON, schema confirmed from sigil/import source code
resolution_path.finding: SigLA encodes word boundaries with THREE-VALUED certainty, not a binary divider. From importer.ml parse_properties, layer options map to Bound.t = Here | Unsure | Not_here:

encoding.]-start: Bound.Not_here — definitely does not start here

resolution_path.significance: Our corpus carries word division as a binary inherited from Douros: a divider is present or it is not. The five D9 conflicts may in several cases be Bound.Unsure in SigLA, i.e. not a disagreement between editors but an acknowledged uncertainty our source flattened.
resolution_path.caveat: SigLA 2021 covered administrative documents only. All five D9 sites are religious (Z-type). Coverage must be checked.
resolution_path.status: specification known; awaiting the data itself

partial_resolution.site: KN Zc 6 — the only D9 site present in SigLA
partial_resolution.finding: SigLA records TEN signs on this line, with position 7 UNREADABLE — sitting exactly at the contested boundary. Neither our source nor Younger records a sign there at all.
partial_resolution.interpretation: The word-division disagreement is not two editors reading the same marks differently. There is an illegible sign at the disputed point, which Younger appears to have treated as a divider and our source to have ignored. This is the D12 defect surfacing inside D9: a flattened uncertainty presented as a confident reading by both witnesses.
partial_resolution.status: KN Zc 6 explained; PK Za 8, PR Za 1, SY Zb 7, HT Zd 157+156 absent from SigLA and still open

divergences.title: AP Za 2: i-na-ja-re-TA vs i-na-ja-re-NU
alt_sources: van Soesbergen, Corpus Vol. II Part I (2022), AP Za 2
divergences.note: Three independent editors read -NU against GORILA's -TA. Van Soesbergen states flatly 'Gor erroneo'. This is a 3-to-1 split against our source, and it falls in the libation formula's final slot, which FORMULA.md already flags as reading-dependent.
divergences.weight: high: 3 editors against 1, in the highest-value genre

divergences.title: Doubtful-reading marks are absent from the corpus entirely
divergences.note: GORILA marks uncertain sign readings with subscript dots; Younger uses underlining; van Soesbergen uses underlining. Our source carries NONE of these. corpus_v1 has a `damage` field for breaks (U+1076B) but no field for reading certainty, so a doubtful sign is indistinguishable from a confident one.
divergences.detected_via: Fraction-sign counts against Corazza et al. 2021 (JAS 125). Most signs track closely (J exactly 137 in both). Sign A709 (L) shows ours 10 against their 1.
divergences.diagnosis: Corazza n.2 lists the doubtful instances they exclude: ]L B B in KH 96, L in PH 7b.1-2, L L in PH 12a, ]F L[ in ZA 7b.8, keeping only ZA 11a.4 as certain. Our ten occurrences fall in KH96, KN49, PH10, PH12a, PH7b, ZA11a - i.e. we count their excluded doubtful readings as certain. KN49 and PH10 are additional and unexplained.
divergences.significance: Corazza build a statistical argument (p = 4e-12) that L is NOT an independent sign, resting on its rarity. On our uncorrected counts L is ten times commoner and that argument would not go through. The discrepancy is entirely an artefact of lost certainty marking.
affects: entropy estimates (H1 counts doubtful readings as real)
the alternation and name-parallel tests, marginally
divergences.adjudicable_by: GORILA plates; or re-ingesting from SigLA which carries certainty
divergences.class: same family as D1 (break markers stripped from the label layer), but for a marker that is absent from ALL layers of our source

resolution_path.source: SigLA JSON, schema confirmed from sigil/import source code
resolution_path.evidence: importer.ml line 5: `type att_label = {sign: string; unsure: bool; meta: Document.Metadata.t} [@@deriving yojson]`. Emitted per attestation to a label JSON file (Document.Attestation.label_ name number).
resolution_path.reading_model: Three-way, from label_of_att: Script.Unreadable | Unclassified -> no label emitted at all; Readable {instance; confidence} -> emitted with unsure = not confidence. So SigLA distinguishes unreadable, unclassified, confident and doubtful, where our corpus has a single undifferentiated state.
resolution_path.status: specification known; awaiting the data itself

resolution.source: SigLA database.js, decoded via a purpose-built OCaml Marshal parser
resolution.note: The certainty field exists exactly as importer.ml specified. 432 of 5144 attestations (8.4%) are either doubtful or unreadable — a category our corpus cannot express at all.

divergences.title: Fraction K: 1/16 (Pope, Younger) against 1/10 (Corazza et al. 2021)
divergences.note: We graded K = 1/16 'secure' on Younger's authority. Corazza et al. derive K = 1/10 by constraint programming, as part of a decimal-sexagesimal subset K = 1/10, L2 = 1/20, L3 = 1/30, L4 = 1/40, L6 = 1/60, which appears in all 48 solutions with the best optimality metric. corpus_v1 now follows Corazza and grades it 'derived'.
divergences.significance: A value we called secure was contested in the current literature. The 'secure' grade came from Younger's summary, not from checking whether it was still held.
divergences.adjudicable_by: Corazza et al. 2021 vs Pope 1960 / Bennett 1980; specialist judgement

_third_witness.source: van Soesbergen, The Decipherment of Minoan Linear A, Vol. II: Corpus of Transliterated Linear A Texts (2nd rev. ed., 2022)
_third_witness.value: An independent third transliteration witness alongside Douros and Younger, carrying a critical apparatus that compares GORILA, Raison-Pope and Brice readings per document.
cautions: Uses Raison-Pope sign numeration, not GORILA AB numbers. Site codes differ: AK for Arkhanes (not ARKH), GR for Khania.
Uses underlining for uncertain readings where GORILA uses subscript dots.

CRITICAL: interleaves Hurrian-hypothesis glosses with transliteration (e.g. 'qa[ = ha[', 'do-161-se = do-ho-se', '154-te = wu-te'). These are the author's decipherment proposal, NOT data, and must be stripped exactly as translatedWords was.
_third_witness.status: not yet ingested; would require a parser for its critical apparatus

_sigla_extraction.method: database.js holds two OCaml Marshal blobs escaped as decimal octets in JS string literals. Field names are absent because Marshal stores records positionally. Decoded with a purpose-built parser (ocaml_marshal.py); record layout recovered structurally and cross-checked against sigil/import/importer.ml.

_sigla_extraction.coverage_note: Extends well beyond the administrative-only state of the 2021 paper: 29 Z-type (religious) documents present, including KN Zc 6 (a D9 site). The other four D9 sites and both PH(?)31 documents are absent.

sweep3_summary.significance: Third independent witness, and the only one carrying reading certainty
sweep3_summary.comparison_basis: GORILA sign NUMBER only. The corpora use different variant conventions for the same sign (ours A100-102 / A028B / A131C and gender variants AB021M/F; SigLA AB100 / AB028 / AB131 / AB021), so series prefix and variant suffix are notation. AB021 vs AB022 remains distinct, as D4 required.
sweep3_summary.finding_fractions: The gap between 91.8% and 95.9% is almost entirely fraction signs. SigLA records 332 fraction tokens against our 447, and A732 (JE) is absent entirely (32 in ours, 0 in SigLA). A palaeographic database indexes drawn sign forms, so composite fractions are plausibly drawn as components or omitted. This is a coverage difference, not a reading conflict, and SigLA should NOT be used to adjudicate fraction counts.
sweep3_summary.finding_certainty: Restricting to SigLA-confident signs does NOT improve agreement (95.9% -> 95.2%, sites 156 -> 171). Our disagreements with SigLA are therefore NOT concentrated in readings SigLA flags as doubtful. D12 is a real defect in our corpus, but it does not explain the residual divergence, and the D9/KN Zc 6 case should not be generalised to the corpus as a whole.
sweep3_summary.finding_no_second_systematic_error: After the D4 correction the substitution tail is flat: no pair recurs more than twice across 666 documents. D4 appears to have been the only systematic sign-mapping error in our source.
